dutch.description: Dutch uses Latin alphabet with 26 letters. Known for its guttural G sound.

oromo.name: Qubee (Oromo Alphabet)
oromo.description: Oromo uses Latin script called Qubee. Spoken primarily in Ethiopia.
oromo.special_notes: Oromo uses Latin script called Qubee. 5 vowel system. C, V, X, Z used mainly in borrowed words.

somali.name: Af Soomaali (Somali Alphabet)
somali.description: Somali uses Latin script. Spoken in Somalia, Ethiopia, Djibouti, and Kenya.
somali.special_notes: C represents pharyngeal sound. No P, V in native words. 5 vowel system.

hadiyaa.name: Hadiyyisa (Hadiyya Alphabet)
hadiyaa.description: Hadiyya uses Ethiopic (Ge'ez) script. Spoken in southern Ethiopia.
hadiyaa.special_notes: Abugida system where each character represents consonant+vowel. 7 vowel orders per consonant.

wolayitta.name: Wolaytta Alphabet
wolayitta.description: Wolaytta uses Ethiopic (Ge'ez) script. Spoken in southern Ethiopia.
wolayitta.special_notes: Also spelled Wolaita/Wolyitta. Abugida system with 7 vowel orders. Used in SNNPR region of Ethiopia.

afar.name: Qafar Alphabet
afar.description: Afar uses Latin script. Spoken in Ethiopia, Eritrea, and Djibouti.
afar.special_notes: Cushitic language. Known for guttural sounds. Latin script adopted in 1970s.

gamo.name: Gamo Alphabet
gamo.description: Gamo uses Ethiopic (Ge'ez) script. Spoken in southern Ethiopia.
gamo.special_notes: Omotic language. Abugida system with 7 vowel orders per consonant.

swahili.name: Kiswahili Alphabet
swahili.description: Swahili uses Latin script. Lingua franca of East Africa.
swahili.special_notes: Bantu language with Arabic influence. 5 vowel system. No Q, X in native words.

kinyarwanda.name: Ikinyarwanda Alphabet
kinyarwanda.description: Kinyarwanda uses Latin script. Official language of Rwanda.
kinyarwanda.special_notes: Bantu language. 5 vowel system. Tonal language with high and low tones.

kirundi.name: Ikirundi Alphabet
kirundi.description: Kirundi uses Latin script. Official language of Burundi.
kirundi.special_notes: Bantu language closely related to Kinyarwanda. 5 vowel system. Tonal language.

luo.name: Dholuo Alphabet
luo.description: Luo uses Latin script. Spoken in Kenya and Tanzania.
luo.special_notes: Nilotic language. Tonal with 4 tones. No F, Q, V, X, Z in native words.

luganda.name: Oluganda Alphabet
luganda.description: Luganda uses Latin script. Spoken in Uganda.
luganda.special_notes: Bantu language. Double consonants indicate gemination. Tonal language.
